scenes.title: Tl
scenes.sub: timelines for Unity DOTS and plain .NET
scenes.text: This is Tl. A timeline library for Unity DOTS, and for plain dot net. Designers draw the timeline. Your code gets plain numbers.

scenes.title: Five pieces, every time
scenes.text: Every effect is the same five pieces. A clip holds the designer's numbers. A track turns a clip into values. A kind combines those values. A column stores the result. And your own system reads it.

scenes.title: Teleport.cs: the whole example
scenes.text: Here is a whole example. A teleport clip. A track that jumps when the clip starts, and comes back when it ends. A kind that adds the jump to a column. That is one file.

scenes.title: Run it
scenes.text: Run it. At tick thirty the player jumps to five. At tick ninety, to thirteen. At tick one nineteen the clip ends, and it comes back to five. The picture is Unity. The numbers are the same in plain dot net.

scenes.title: Stats and buffs over time
scenes.text: Stats and buffs, over time. Hits and poison drain health. A haste clip adds attack while it plays, and a second start replaces the first, so the bonus never stacks.

scenes.title: Inventory, with rewind
scenes.text: Inventory. Loot fills the bag, and a craft clip turns wood into planks. Now rewind. The bag is empty again, because every pulse is signed by the direction of play. Play it again, and it fills the same way.

scenes.title: Force: a push, and the way back
scenes.text: Force. One clip pushes the cube to the right, about four metres, and slows it down. A second timeline pushes it back to zero. The number beside the video is the cube's real x, recorded from Unity.

scenes.title: Control: a clip that starts a clip

stat.sub: where the dash ends, as the test expects

scenes.text: Control. A clip watches the cube. When it passes two metres, it starts a dash timeline, and the cube moves along z. The dash ends exactly where the test expects.

scenes.title: Events: a clip raises an event
scenes.text: Events. Each strike clip makes the knight lunge, and at the moment it starts, it raises an event. Gameplay code sends damage to the dummy, squashes it, and spawns a spark. Fifteen strikes, fifteen sparks.

scenes.title: Motion: values over time
scenes.text: Motion. No game code. The cube glides, the sphere breathes and changes colour, and the capsule spins while it hops. A plain dot net program samples the same timeline, and all forty eight ninety seven samples match.

scenes.title: Crowd: ten thousand dancers

stat.sub: per entity per tick at 100,000, 0 bytes

scenes.text: Crowd. Ten thousand dancers, each started on its own tick, so the field ripples. A hundred thousand cost about thirty three nanoseconds per entity per tick, and allocate zero bytes.

scenes.text: To try it, run the installer. It builds a Unity project, imports every demo, and runs each demo's test. Seven demos. Nine tests. All passing.
